recipes.name: Air-Fryer Vanjaram Masala Fry

steps.text: Pat the steaks dry and make two shallow slits on each side.
Mix chilli powder, turmeric, pepper, grated ginger, lemon juice, rice flour, salt and garlic oil into a thick paste; coat the steaks on both sides and rest.
Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Brush the basket with a few drops of groundnut oil and lay the steaks flat in one layer.
Air-fry at 200°C for 6 minutes, then flip carefully with a flat spatula.
Scatter curry leaves on top, brush with the remaining oil and air-fry another 5–6 minutes until the edges char like a tawa fry.
Rest 1 minute and serve with lemon wedges and sliced onion or cucumber.

tips: Rice flour gives the tawa-style crust without semolina; keep the paste thick so it clings.
For an IBS flare day skip the onion on the side and serve with cucumber.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate up to 8 hours ahead and refrigerate; air-fry just before eating.

recipes.name: Chettinad Seer Fish Curry

ingredients.note: soaked in 300 ml warm water, pulp extracted

steps.text: Heat gingelly oil in a kadai; splutter mustard, fenugreek and fennel seeds, then add curry leaves.
Add shallots and garlic and sauté until golden.
Add tomato with chilli, coriander, turmeric and pepper; cook until the oil separates.
Pour in the tamarind water plus 200 ml water and salt; boil until it thickens slightly and loses the raw tamarind smell.
Slide in the fish steaks, shake the kadai (do not stir) and simmer on low until the fish is just cooked.
Rest off the heat for at least 10 minutes so the gravy soaks into the fish.

tips: Kuzhambu tastes best the next day — tamarind keeps it safe to reheat.
recipes.makeAhead: Make the gravy base (up to step 4) 2 days ahead; add fish on the day.

recipes.name: Kerala Seer Fish Moilee

steps.text: Rub the fish with turmeric, pepper, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Sear the steaks in half the coconut oil for 1 minute per side; remove.
In the remaining oil sauté whole spices, ginger, garlic, green chilli, onion and curry leaves until soft but not brown.
Add the thin coconut milk and salt; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and tomato rounds and simmer on low until the fish flakes.
Pour in the thick coconut milk, warm through without boiling and turn off the heat.

tips: Never boil after adding thick coconut milk — it splits.
Serve with a small portion of red rice or appam.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Fish Tikka

steps.text: Rub the cubes with lemon juice and half the salt.
Whisk hung curd with ginger, garlic, chilli, garam masala, cumin, kasuri methi, mustard oil and the remaining salt; fold in fish and capsicum gently and marinate.
Thread onto short skewers or lay directly in the lined air-fryer basket, leaving gaps.
Air-fry at 200°C for 6 minutes, flip each piece, and air-fry 5–6 minutes more until charred at the edges.
Sprinkle chaat masala or lemon and serve with mint chutney.

tips: Seer holds its shape best; avoid soft fish for tikka.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate up to 6 hours in the fridge.

recipes.name: Goan Fish Curry

steps.text: Grind coconut, red chillies, coriander, cumin, turmeric, garlic, ginger and tamarind with water to a very smooth paste.
Heat oil in a pot, sauté onion until translucent, then add tomato and green chilli and cook soft.
Add the masala paste, 300 ml water and salt; simmer until the raw smell goes.
Add kokum and the fish slices, shake the pot to coat and simmer gently without stirring.
Rest covered for 10 minutes before serving.

tips: Keep coconut to the stated amount — the colour comes from Kashmiri chillies, not extra coconut.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Pomfret Recheado

ingredients.note: 2 whole (≈250 g each), cleaned, slit along the backbone for stuffing

steps.text: Grind the vinegar-soaked chillies with garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, spices, turmeric, jaggery and salt to a thick recheado paste (no water).
Stuff the paste into the slits and rub over both sides of the pomfret; marinate.
Preheat the air fryer to 190°C, line with perforated parchment and brush with oil.
Air-fry the pomfret at 190°C for 8 minutes, brush with oil, flip carefully with a wide spatula.
Air-fry another 7–8 minutes until the masala is crisp and the flesh near the bone is opaque.

tips: Recheado paste keeps 2 weeks refrigerated — make a jar and use for prawns too.
recipes.makeAhead: Paste can be made a week ahead.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Tandoori Pomfret

ingredients.note: 2 whole, cleaned, 3 deep diagonal slashes per side

steps.text: Rub the fish with lemon juice, salt and half the ginger-garlic for the first marinade.
Mix hung curd, chilli, garam masala, cumin, kasuri methi, mustard oil and remaining ginger-garlic; coat the fish, pushing into the slashes.
Air-fry at 200°C on a greased rack for 8 minutes, then flip.
Baste with any remaining marinade and air-fry 6–8 minutes more until charred.
Serve with onion rings, lemon and mint chutney.

tips: A double marinade (acid first, curd second) keeps the pomfret firm.

recipes.name: Kerala Pomfret Pollichathu

steps.text: Marinate the pomfret with chilli, turmeric, pepper, lemon and a little salt.
Shallow-fry the fish in half the coconut oil on a tawa for 2 minutes per side until half-cooked; set aside.
In the same oil sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves; add tomato and cook to a thick masala.
Stir in thick coconut milk and remaining salt; cook until it coats the spoon.
Spread masala on wilted banana leaf, place the fish, cover with more masala and fold into a parcel.
Cook parcels on a covered tawa on low heat, flipping once halfway.

tips: Wilt banana leaves over a flame so they fold without tearing; foil works in a pinch.

recipes.name: Steamed Mustard Pomfret Parcels

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds with green chilli, coconut, salt and a splash of water to a smooth paste; rest so the bitterness mellows.
Stir turmeric, lemon juice and raw mustard oil into the paste and coat the fish pieces.
Wrap each piece in banana leaf (or parchment) with a slit green chilli on top; tie with thread.
Steam over rapidly boiling water until the fish is opaque.
Open at the table and drizzle a few drops of raw mustard oil.

tips: Grind mustard with a pinch of salt and green chilli to avoid bitterness.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Mangalorean Mackerel Rava Fry

steps.text: Grind Byadgi chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, turmeric and salt into a thick red masala.
Rub masala deep into the slits and inside the cavity; marinate.
Press each mackerel into rice rava on both sides and spray or brush generously with coconut oil.
Air-fry at 200°C for 7 minutes, flip and brush the other side with oil.
Air-fry 6–7 minutes more until the rava is golden and crunchy.

tips: Rice rava stays crisper than semolina and is wheat-free.

recipes.name: Kundapur Tangy Mackerel Curry

ingredients.note: 3 whole, cleaned, cut into thick pieces

steps.text: Grind red chillies, tamarind, turmeric, coriander, pepper and ginger with 100 ml water into a smooth sour-spicy paste.
Bring the paste to a boil in a clay pot or kadai with 200 ml water and salt.
Add mackerel pieces and simmer uncovered, shaking the pan, until the gravy is thick and coats the fish.
Temper crushed garlic and curry leaves in hot coconut oil and pour over the curry.
Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

tips: Pulimunchi means sour-hot — no coconut in the gravy, so it stays light.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; flavour deepens overnight.

recipes.name: Air-Fried Lemon-Pepper Mackerel Bowl

steps.text: Rub the fillets with pepper, turmeric, half the lemon juice, garlic oil and a pinch of salt.
Air-fry skin side down at 200°C for 6 minutes, flip, then 4 minutes more until the skin crisps.
Toss lettuce, cucumber, tomato, carrot and coriander with olive oil, remaining lemon, roasted cumin and salt.
Flake the hot mackerel over the salad and serve immediately.

tips: Mackerel is one of the richest omega-3 sources available at Indian fish markets.

recipes.name: Goan Mackerel Xacuti

ingredients.note: 3 whole, cleaned, cut into 3 pieces each

steps.text: Dry-roast red chillies, coriander, whole spices, pepper and fennel until aromatic.
In a little oil roast onion and grated coconut until deep brown; grind with the roasted spices, garlic, turmeric and tamarind to a fine paste.
Fry the paste in the remaining oil until it darkens and releases oil.
Add 300 ml water and salt; simmer to a medium-thick gravy.
Add mackerel and simmer gently until cooked through, shaking the kadai instead of stirring.

tips: The deep roast of the coconut is what makes xacuti — brown, not black.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Kerala Sardine Fry

ingredients.note: 8–10 whole, cleaned, heads off, 2 slits per side

steps.text: Make a thick paste of chilli, turmeric, pepper, ginger, lemon juice, garlic oil and salt.
Rub into the sardines, including the slits and cavity, and marinate.
Lay curry leaves on the oiled air-fryer tray and place sardines on top in a single layer.
Air-fry at 200°C for 6 minutes, brush with coconut oil, flip.
Air-fry 5–6 minutes more until crisp at the tail.

tips: Eat the small bones — sardines are an excellent calcium source.

recipes.name: Kerala Sardine Red Curry

steps.text: Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or kadai; add fenugreek, then shallots, ginger, garlic and curry leaves and sauté.
Lower the heat, add chilli, coriander and turmeric with a splash of water and cook without burning.
Add tomato, kokum with its soaking water, 250 ml water and salt; boil.
Arrange the sardines in a single layer and simmer covered on low.
Swirl the pot, drizzle a little coconut oil and rest at least 30 minutes before eating.

tips: Traditionally made a day ahead — it gets better in the fridge.

recipes.name: Sardine with Coconut & Kokum

steps.text: Coarsely crush coconut, ginger, green chilli and turmeric without water.
Spread half the coconut mix in a kadai, layer sardines and spinach, then top with the rest, kokum, curry leaves and salt.
Add 120 ml water, cover tightly and cook on low until the water is almost absorbed.
Drizzle coconut oil, uncover and cook 3 minutes more to dry it out.

tips: Coconut stays at 25 g per serving here, within the low-FODMAP limit.

recipes.name: Bengali Light Rohu Curry

steps.text: Rub the rohu with turmeric and salt.
Sear the fish in smoking mustard oil until lightly golden on both sides; remove.
In the same oil splutter cumin seeds, fry potato and brinjal wedges until edges colour.
Add ginger, cumin powder, chilli and tomato; cook until soft.
Add 400 ml hot water and green chilli; simmer until potatoes are tender.
Return the fish and simmer 4 minutes; finish with coriander.

tips: A thin jhol is the everyday Bengali fish curry — no onion or garlic needed.

recipes.name: Rohu in Mustard Gravy

steps.text: Grind soaked mustard seeds with 4 green chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub rohu with turmeric and salt and lightly fry in mustard oil until golden; set aside.
Temper the oil with nigella/cumin and slit green chillies, add tomato and cook briefly.
Add mustard paste mixed with 250 ml water, bring to a gentle simmer (do not boil hard).
Add the fish, simmer covered until the gravy thickens, and drizzle raw mustard oil.

tips: Boiling mustard paste hard makes it bitter — keep it at a gentle simmer.

recipes.name: Andhra Tamarind Fish Curry

steps.text: Marinate fish with a little chilli, turmeric and salt.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves, then sauté onion and green chilli until golden.
Add ginger-garlic, tomato, chilli powder, coriander and turmeric; cook to a thick masala.
Pour in tamarind pulp with 300 ml water, jaggery and salt; boil until the gravy turns glossy.
Slide in the fish, sprinkle ground fenugreek and simmer uncovered without stirring.
Turn off and rest — pulusu is best eaten a few hours later.

tips: Andhra homes make pulusu in the morning for dinner; the fish soaks up the sour gravy.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Amritsari Fish

steps.text: Toss the fingers with lemon juice, salt and ginger-garlic.
Mix besan, rice flour, chilli, ajwain/cumin and garam masala with a few spoons of water and half the oil into a thick batter; coat the fish.
Arrange in the oiled air-fryer basket without touching and brush tops with oil.
Air-fry at 200°C for 6 minutes, flip and brush again.
Air-fry 5–6 minutes more until golden; dust with chaat masala.

tips: A coating of mostly rice flour (with a little besan) keeps it crisp and gentler on IBS.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Salmon Tikka

steps.text: Mix hung curd, ginger, spices, kasuri methi, lemon, garlic oil, mustard oil and salt.
Fold in the salmon cubes and marinate in the fridge.
Air-fry at 200°C for 5 minutes, flip each cube.
Air-fry 4–5 minutes more until just opaque inside and charred outside.
Serve with cucumber raita or lemon wedges.

tips: Salmon is already fatty — no extra oil needed beyond the marinade.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Garlic-Pepper Salmon

steps.text: Toss salmon with half the soy sauce, half the pepper and cornflour.
Air-fry at 200°C for 5 minutes, shake/flip, then 3–4 minutes more until crisp-edged.
Meanwhile heat garlic oil in a pan, stir-fry ginger, green chilli and capsicum on high heat.
Add remaining soy, vinegar, pepper and a splash of water, toss in the salmon and spring onion greens.
Serve hot over lettuce or a small portion of rice.

tips: Garlic-infused oil gives the garlic flavour without fructans.

recipes.name: Salmon & Egg Bhurji

steps.text: Heat garlic oil, sauté ginger, green chilli and spring onion greens.
Add tomato, turmeric and salt and cook until soft; stir in spinach until wilted.
Add flaked salmon and stir gently to warm through.
Pour in beaten eggs and scramble on low heat until just set; finish with pepper and coriander.

tips: Uses leftover fish from dinner — a fast high-protein breakfast.

recipes.name: Grilled Salmon Kachumber Bowl

steps.text: Cook the rice and spread it to cool.
Rub salmon with cumin, chilli, half the lemon juice, salt and 2 g oil.
Grill on a hot grill pan skin side down 4 minutes, flip, 3 minutes more (or air-fry at 200°C for 8 minutes without flipping).
Toss cucumber, tomato, capsicum, mint, coriander with remaining lemon, oil and salt.
Build bowls: lettuce, rice, kachumber, then the salmon on top.

tips: Cooled rice has more resistant starch — easier on blood sugar.

recipes.name: Kerala Prawn Roast

steps.text: Marinate prawns with half the chilli, turmeric and salt.
Fry coconut slivers in coconut oil until golden; remove.
Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves until deep golden.
Add tomato and remaining powders; cook until oil separates.
Add prawns and roast on high heat, tossing, until the masala coats them dry.
Finish with pepper, garam masala and the fried coconut.

tips: Do not overcook prawns — they turn rubbery after 6–7 minutes.

recipes.name: Goan Prawn Balchão

steps.text: Grind vinegar-soaked chillies with garlic, ginger, cumin, spices, pepper and turmeric into a smooth balchão paste.
Toss prawns in salt and turmeric and sear in half the oil for 2 minutes; remove.
Fry onion in the remaining oil until golden, add tomato and cook down.
Add the paste and jaggery and fry until the oil rises.
Return the prawns and cook until the masala is thick and clinging.
Cool and rest — balchão tastes best after a day.

tips: Vinegar preserves it; refrigerated it keeps up to a week.
recipes.makeAhead: Make 1–2 days ahead; keeps 5–7 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Prawn Koliwada

steps.text: Toss prawns with lemon, salt and ginger-garlic.
Add besan, rice flour, chilli, ajwain and 1 tbsp oil with a splash of water to make a clingy coating.
Air-fry at 200°C in one layer for 5 minutes, brush with oil, flip.
Air-fry 4–5 minutes until crisp and golden; serve with lemon and green chutney.

tips: Tail-on prawns are easy to pick up as party bites.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chilli Prawns

steps.text: Toss prawns with half the soy sauce, pepper and cornflour.
Air-fry at 200°C for 4 minutes, shake/flip, then 3 minutes more until crisp-edged.
Heat garlic oil in a pan or wok until hot; stir-fry ginger, green chilli and capsicum for 2 minutes.
Add remaining soy, chilli sauce, vinegar and 2 tbsp water; bubble until glossy.
Toss in the prawns and spring onion greens and serve immediately.

tips: Keep capsicum crunchy — high heat, quick toss.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chettinad Prawn Pepper Fry

steps.text: Dry-roast pepper, fennel, cumin and red chilli for a minute and grind coarsely.
Coat prawns with the spice powder, turmeric, ginger, garlic oil, lemon and salt.
Air-fry at 200°C for 4 minutes, shake/flip, then 3–4 minutes more.
Heat sesame oil in a pan, crackle curry leaves, toss in the prawns for 1 minute to coat.

tips: Naturally low-FODMAP and keto — no onion, no garlic cloves.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Mangalorean Prawn Ghee Roast

steps.text: Grind soaked chillies, roasted coriander, cumin, pepper, fenugreek, garlic, tamarind and jaggery into a fine paste.
Marinate prawns with curd, salt and 1 tbsp of the paste.
Air-fry at 200°C for 4 minutes, flip, then 3 minutes more.
Heat ghee in a pan, fry the remaining paste on low until deep red and fragrant.
Toss in the prawns and curry leaves for 1–2 minutes until glazed.

tips: Air-frying first means the dish needs a third of the usual ghee.

recipes.name: Prawn Masala Omelette

steps.text: Sauté prawns in half the garlic oil with ginger, turmeric and a pinch of salt until pink.
Beat eggs and whites with tomato, spring onion greens, chilli, pepper, coriander and salt.
Heat remaining oil in a pan, pour in half the egg, scatter half the prawns and cook covered on low.
Fold or flip and cook 1 minute more; repeat for the second omelette.

tips: Spring onion greens replace onion for a low-FODMAP breakfast.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Tandoori Prawn Salad Bowl

steps.text: Mix hung curd, ginger-garlic, chilli, garam masala, half the lemon, mustard oil and salt; coat prawns.
Air-fry at 200°C for 4 minutes, flip, then 3–4 minutes more until charred.
Toss lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion and mint with olive oil, remaining lemon and a pinch of salt.
Top with the hot prawns and serve.

tips: Use lactose-free curd and skip onion rings for the IBS-safe bowl.
